chunks: So, leave them until they face their day (of doom) when they will be stunned.

key_terms.يُصْعَقُونَ: They will be stunned or struck with awe

ai.seo_question: What does the term 'yus'qoon' mean in the context of the Day of Judgment in Surah Al-Mursalat?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the divine patience (hilm) granted to the disbelievers, allowing them to experience the full weight of their denial before the sudden, overwhelming shock (su'q) of the Hereafter. The term 'su'q' is interpreted not merely as fear, but as a state of being struck dumb or paralyzed by the magnitude of truth, serving as the ultimate consequence of their persistent rejection of the Prophetic message.
